title: ISLAMICLEGALBENCH: EVALUATING LLMS KNOWLEDGE AND REASONING OF ISLAMIC LAW ACROSS 1,200 YEARS OF ISLAMIC PLURALIST LEGAL TRADITIONS
measurement_description: The paper evaluates Large Language Models on their knowledge and reasoning capabilities regarding Islamic law (fiqh) and jurisprudence across seven schools of thought, covering over 1,200 years of legal traditions. It measures model correctness, hallucination rates, abstention behavior, and susceptibility to sycophancy (false premise detection) across tasks of varying complexity.
findings: Current LLMs lack adequate foundational Islamic legal knowledge and are not ready for reliable deployment in religious advisory contexts. The best model achieved only 67.65% correctness with a 21.25% hallucination rate, while weaker models failed significantly and hallucinated over 55% of the time. Few-shot prompting provided almost no improvement. The evaluation revealed a 'Mid-Complexity Failure Zone' where models failed on tasks requiring exact, text-anchored doctrinal recall but appeared falsely competent on complex reasoning tasks due to semantic generalization. Many models also exhibited dangerous sycophantic behavior by confidently accepting and justifying false religious premises.
